integration.api: No vendor API - this is a raw mini-LVDS panel. You supply the driving stack. Two documented routes: (1) Good Display's own 25.3" TCON board plus Android system motherboard, which ships with an SDK and takes images from a USB drive prepared by a Windows tool, or over Wi-Fi/Bluetooth; (2) the open-source Modos Caster/Glider FPGA controller, whose documentation explicitly covers the LVDS signalling used on 'higher resolution panels (such as 25.3" ones ...)'.
integration.custom_software: Entirely yours. Nothing to sideload around - you own the whole stack from framebuffer to waveform.
integration.community: Modos Caster/Glider (CERN-OHL, GitLab/GitHub mirrors) is the only open controller documented as reaching this panel class. EPDiy, the other well-known open ESP32 e-paper driver, tops out around 13.3" and its README lists nothing above ~7.8-13.3" and no Spectra 6 support.
integration.notes: This is the highest-resolution >15 in colour e-paper panel found anywhere in this survey at 163 PPI - substantially sharper than every 31.5" option (~93 PPI) and sharper than the 28.5" A2 panels (~131 PPI). For a fine-art application that is the single most important spec, and it makes this panel the best raw substrate available. Two hard caveats. FIRST, an important and under-appreciated compatibility risk: Caster's own documentation says it 'supports electrophoretic display panels with parallel I/F (Eink, OED and DES)' and is 'compatible with both monochrome and color-filter-array based screens'. Spectra 6 is NOT a colour-filter-array device - it is a four-pigment microcup system needing its own multi-pass waveform set. So Caster driving this panel's LVDS timing is documented, but Caster rendering correct Spectra 6 COLOUR is not, and would likely need new waveform work. Treat 'open controller drives the 25.3" in full colour' as INFERENCE, not fact, until demonstrated. SECOND, Glider's README notes a constraint that X resolution multiplied by Y resolution must be a multiple of 128; 3200 x 1800 = 5,760,000, which divides by 128 exactly (45,000), so this panel does satisfy it. The pragmatic route for a determined builder is Good Display's own TCON plus Android motherboard with SDK, which is a known-good colour stack, and to treat the open FPGA path as a research project.

art_suitability.gamut_notes: 163 PPI, 4,096 colours, 85% NTSC, ~30:1 contrast, anti-glare glass. Best pixel density above 15 in that this survey found. Because Spectra 6 reaches intermediate colours by dithering, high PPI matters disproportionately here - dither noise is what limits perceived quality, and 163 PPI hides it far better than 93 PPI. Operating range 0-50 C; storage -25 to 60 C.
art_suitability.ghosting: Not documented by the vendor. integration.custom_software: Fully. Flow presents as a standard USB-C DisplayPort monitor to Linux, macOS and Windows, so any local application drives it with no vendor involvement whatsoever. integration.notes: Openness here is in a different league from every commercial vendor in this survey - CERN-OHL licensed hardware, published schematics, open gateware, a real host API, and an as-a-monitor path that needs no integration work at all. This is the clearest instance of the pattern the brief asked to be called out: Modos wins criterion 2 outright and loses criterion 1 badly, being a two-person company. THE SIZE PROBLEM, stated plainly: the Dev Kit's Glider Mega Adapter covers 4.3" to 13.3" only - the published adapter list ends at 13.3" (ES133UTx/ED133UTx/EC133UJ1) and 11.3" (ED113TCx), and the campaign says 'Compatible with a wide range of screens - from 6-inch up to 13.3-inch'. Flow itself is marked 'Works With Other Panels: No'; only the Dev Kit is 'Yes'. So there is no ready-made Modos product above 15 in. The path that exists is: buy the 13" Dev Kit for its Caster driver board, and drive a 25.3" LVDS panel per the Glider documentation - a bring-up project, not a purchase.

For colour art reproduction Kaleido 3 is the weaker technology; for monochrome/graphite/etching reproduction at 300 PPI it is the best option in this entire survey. Amber-tinted frontlight is available, which is a colour-accuracy negative for art viewing.
art_suitability.ghosting: Actively engineered against - hybrid binary-then-16-level-greyscale mode updates fast first and refines to greyscale as the image settles, explicitly to minimise latency and visual flashing. vendors.country: United States - 867 Boylston St., Boston, MA 02116
vendors.ownership: Founder-owned. Two named founders: Alexander Soto and Wenting Zhang.

Campaign 2 (Flow) raised USD 713,276 against a USD 175,000 goal - 407% - from 609 backers, funded 2026-07-09. Cumulative crowdfunding raised is roughly USD 0.9M.
vendors.revenue_scale: Inferable only from campaign totals - under USD 1M lifetime. No commercial revenue disclosed.
vendors.headcount: Two (the two founders). IEEE Spectrum describes it explicitly as a 'two-person startup'.
vendors.hardware_track_record: One product designed, manufactured and shipped: the Paper Dev Kit, funded September 2025, first shipment starting February 2026, with shipping/case/firmware progress updates through April 2026 and the 13 in kit now marked In stock. Certifications completed. A second product (Flow) has passed pre-production revisions with validation and testing done, contract manufacturers in China contracted, full BoM, supplier quotes and tooling in place, panels sourced directly from E Ink, and fulfilment via Crowd Supply's partner Mouser Electronics. Documented the whole journey publicly through conference talks at FOSDEM 2024, Supercon 2024, Latch-up 2024 and FOSDEM 2026.
vendors.abandonment_history: None found. The opposite pattern is evidenced: 11 public updates on campaign 1 including post-delivery firmware progress, 7 on campaign 2, a public issue tracker, published changelogs and versioned firmware releases. Their own risk statement concedes that development timelines typically need doubling, and delivery did run from a September 2025 funding to a February 2026 first shipment.
vendors.rationale: BLUNT ASSESSMENT: this is a two-person company with under USD 1M of lifetime crowdfunding revenue, no institutional investment, a grant from a public-interest fund, and exactly one product delivered to date. On a three-year horizon the probability that Modos Tech still exists as a going concern is materially below that of any incorporated competitor here, and the client should not plan a hardware dependency on the company continuing. HOWEVER - and this is the case the brief asked to be made explicitly - the staying-power question is much less damaging for Modos than for any other low-durability vendor in this survey, because everything that matters is already published under open licences: Caster gateware under CERN-OHL-P, Glider hardware under CERN-OHL-S, firmware under MIT, a host API with Python/Rust/C bindings, full schematics and design files, and 2.5k GitHub stars on Glider with 301 on Caster. If Modos folds tomorrow, the design survives and remains buildable and maintainable by third parties. That is the precise inverse of the InkPoster or Samsung risk profile, where the company will very likely persist but the device is unmaintainable by anyone outside it. Modos wins criterion 2 outright and loses criterion 1 outright, and the openness genuinely mitigates the corporate fragility in a way it does not for anyone else here.

leads_not_followed.why_promising: The only >15in colour reflective displays found that are NOT built on E Ink panels, at 28", 31.5" and 55", with claimed sub-1-second refresh and up to 16 million colours - and the vendor itself names art galleries as a target market. If the resolution and reflectance are respectable this would break the E Ink single-supply dependency entirely. But no resolution figure is published anywhere on the site, and ChLCD is characteristically desaturated, so this needs measured data before it can be taken seriously.

leads_not_followed.what: Agile (E Ink ecosystem partner) - the 75" Kaleido 3 display and the 'Agile Conversion Engine' middleware
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Agile built a 75" Kaleido 3 display with E Ink and supplies conversion middleware. Kaleido 3 at large size is a different colour technology from Spectra 6 (colour-filter-array over monochrome, faster refresh, lower saturation, higher effective mono resolution), and a middleware layer implies a documented content pipeline. Worth investigating as an alternative colour approach and as a possible source of image-conversion tooling. Named on E Ink's InfoComm page but Agile's own site was not reached.

leads_not_followed.what: Fraimic's local-only mode protocol, and the backers-only campaign updates
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Fraimic advertises the strongest local-only claim of any consumer frame ('no third-party servers', 'No apps | No subscriptions') yet also requires an account at app.fraimic.com, and publishes no protocol. Most substantive updates (#10-#13, #15) are backers-only, so delivery quality and the local-mode mechanics are unverifiable from outside. If the local mode turns out to be a documented HTTP endpoint rather than a manual browser upload, the 31.5" Large Canvas at USD 1,299 becomes a much stronger candidate than currently rated.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Visionect has any colour (Spectra 6 or Kaleido) product on its roadmap
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Visionect's self-hosted RESTful JSON API with programmatic control of dithering method and bit-depth encoding is precisely the architecture this client needs, and its Place & Play 32" is in stock at EUR 2,300 - but it is monochrome, which disqualifies it for colour art. A colour Visionect model would immediately become the leading candidate in this entire survey. Worth a direct enquiry.

leads_not_followed.what: Independent measurement of Spectra 6 colour accuracy, gamut and ghosting at large sizes for art reproduction
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The single biggest evidence gap across every device in this slice. Not one vendor documents a colour profile, none publishes measured gamut, and no vendor or reviewer publishes ghosting characterisation for the large panels. All that exists are platform-level marketing figures (4,096 colours, ~85% NTSC, ~30:1 contrast, <=15s full refresh). For an archive of gigapixel scans where reproduction fidelity is the whole point, this needs resolving empirically - most likely by buying one panel or frame and measuring it, since the published record will not answer it.

leads_not_followed.what: Seeed Studio XIAO ePaper DIY Kit EE02 and Soldered Inkplate 13Spectra - 13.3" Spectra 6 open dev boards
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both are below the 15in floor so they are out of scope as targets, but both are ESP32-S3 open development boards for Spectra 6 colour panels with published toolchains. They are the cheapest way to prototype and validate the client's rendering, dithering and colour-conversion pipeline against real Spectra 6 hardware before committing to an expensive large panel - a genuinely useful de-risking step.
